answer: A bonded reputation registry resists Sybils by making each identity costly: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and build verifiable history of completed work before transacting at scale. Creating thousands of fakes then requires thousands of deposits, while misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the history, so attackers pay linearly per fake. Like shale laid down layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly; a newcomer at the wharf cannot fake years of juniper trade checks overnight, because each attested delivery adds a layer that cannot be copied cheaply.
